summary: What a page may call on window.SF. A public name keeps its meaning and is renamed or removed only through the change journal, as an attribute is; an internal one is the runtime's and may change in any release. tests/browser/public-js-api.browser.mjs holds the list against the runtime: every name the runtime puts on window.SF is here, and every public name and member the probe loads is there. A component's script API (SF.Input, SF.Carousel, ...) arrives with its component and is listed with it. loaded_by says when a name exists: core -- as soon as core.js has run, before the next script on the page; core-loader -- when the Loader has started, at the window event sf-loader-init (core.js loads it); smart-base -- when the Smart base has loaded (SF.loadSmartBase(), or the first Smart element on the page); component/<name>, smart/<name> -- with that component. The probe takes the names at each of those moments (documentation trial 6, 2026-10-18: the Loader's names were listed under core). layer and doc say where the documentation lists a name (owner decision D17, 2026-11-11): layer is core, loader, smart-base or component -- the documentation's Functions section lists the Framework's own names grouped by the first three, and a component's script API (layer component) is documented on its component's page; doc is public (listed for authors) or internal (not listed). Both are derived from loaded_by and status by scripts/generate-public-js-api-layers.mjs, whose exception table says why a name differs; public-js-api.schema.json is the shape.

globals.name: SF.Loader
globals.summary: The runtime loader: loads what a page uses, components and utilities, on demand, and the theme. ensure(tags, {timeout}) asks for elements and settles with {ready, missing}, never rejecting; watch(root) marks a box an element renders into as a portal the Loader reads as the page (unwatch unmarks it). Once a theme is set (setTheme, changeTheme), SF.Loader.theme and SF.Loader.themePreference read it.

globals.name: SF.RuleLoader
globals.summary: The load rules by name: what a class, a tag or a component needs. A component set adds its own rules here (its rule.js) with SF.RuleLoader.registerPackage(name, {rules, api, aliases, exports, base}); SF.RuleLoader.packageOf(name) answers where a set is served ({name, base, declared, registered, version, release, api, exported}, frozen). Both are functions, not rules, and are not enumerated (since core.runtime 1.25.0).

globals.name: SF.Preferences
globals.summary: The person's view preferences: kept in this browser and, when the host keeps them, for the person (simai.interaction-rules).

globals.name: SF.RegionNavigation
globals.summary: Moves between pages by swapping the content region, not the page (simai.interface-fragment).

globals.name: SF.workspace
globals.summary: The workspace layout's controller for an .sf-workspace element: show('list' | 'main') sets the narrow view, panel(open) opens or closes the panel (a column when wide, a drawer below); view, panelOpen and layout read the state. The events sf-workspace-view {view} and sf-workspace-panel {open} fire on the element (docs/developer/workspace-layout.md).

globals.name: SF.Composition
globals.summary: The composition helpers: fragment descriptors, the page host's outputs, registries of component types and ports, field kinds and the words of the built-in editor manifests (editorFieldMessages; owner sf-composition in SF.language); since core.runtime 1.23.0 the one block editor's contracts: the catalogue and variants, layout parameters as utilities, own modifiers, site blocks, named places and the data source port (docs/developer/block-author-guide.md); since core.runtime 1.26.0 the catalogue's groups with their icons and words (CATALOGUE_GROUP_TABLE, Elements and Layout replace Structure, a dated alias until 2027-01-01), each built-in type's icon, and parameter defaults a type prints unset (effectiveProps); since core.runtime 1.27.0 a type in more than one section (catalogue.also_in, BUILTIN_CATALOGUE_ALSO_IN, entryGroups; catalogue() gives sections), the built-in form types and the accent background.

globals.name: SF.Effects
globals.summary: Background effects (simai.effect): check a manifest, read stored settings, resolve a placement's theme, mount an effect or a windows group under the rules, load one from the pinned catalogue with integrity, run a foreign one only in a sandboxed frame. Since core.runtime 1.25.0 a dated alias of the set effects: the engine lives in simai/ui-effects, SF.package('effects') answers the same functions, and every read of SF.Effects is noted in SF.deprecations (journal global-sf-effects-to-package, remove_after 2027-01-01).

globals.name: SF.package
globals.summary: A component set's scripted API: SF.package('<set>') is a Promise of what the set's bundle registered as its exports (SF.RuleLoader.registerPackage(name, {exports})), asking for the set's api element when it has not loaded. Rejects when the page has not declared the set, naming the line to add (data-sf-sets on the core script, or SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.<set>). Callable as soon as core.js has run; it waits for the Loader (since core.runtime 1.25.0).

globals.name: SF.Position

globals.name: SF.Mask

globals.name: SF.notify

globals.name: SF.notifications

globals.name: SF.sanitizeHtml
globals.summary: Cleans untrusted HTML into a DocumentFragment from an allowlist: SF.sanitizeHtml(html, {elements?, codeLanguage?, document?}). Scripts and foreign content are dropped with their content, other unknown elements unwrapped, and only safe links and table spans kept.

globals.name: SF.safeHref
globals.summary: The href SF.sanitizeHtml keeps, or null: http, https and mailto URLs and root-relative paths, never //host or /\host.

globals.name: SF.format
globals.summary: Dates, days, numbers and file sizes in the page's language (the locale named, else the node's page language), through Intl. date(value, {date, time, intl, locale, node}); relativeDay(value, {now, today, yesterday, tomorrow, weekday, capital}) says today, yesterday, a weekday of the last week or the date, and msUntilNextDay(now) when that changes; relativeTime(value, {now}); dayOffset(value, {now}) counts calendar days; number(value, format, {step, grouping, gap}) by a format word (number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent, compact, currency-<CODE>, unit-<unit>); fileSize(size, {units}) in B, KB, MB, GB. docs/developer/format.md.

globals.name: SF.breakpoints
globals.summary: The Framework's breakpoint ladder for scripts, the same steps the sheets switch at (xs 0, sm 32rem, md 44rem, lg 60rem, xl 72rem, xxl 80rem): ladder; query(name, {below}) the media query; media(name, {below}) its MediaQueryList; matches(name, {below}) whether the page is that wide now. docs/developer/format.md.

globals.name: SF.copyText
globals.summary: Copies text: SF.copyText(text, {document}) settles with 'native' (the Clipboard API) or 'legacy' (execCommand over a hidden field, where the API is absent or refused), or rejects (copy_unsupported, or the platform's NotAllowedError). The copy sf-copy-button and the clipboard class make. docs/developer/format.md.

globals.name: SF.codeCopy
globals.summary: Copy on click for code in running text, opt-in with data-sf-code-copy on a container (owner 2026-11-07, R024): refresh(root) marks the code under root that copies and unmarks what no longer should (added and changed containers are followed on their own); copy(code) copies one code's text with SF.copyText and says so in sf-button-copy's words, settling true when copied; isCopyable(code) answers whether a code is a copy control. docs/developer/typography-5.4.md.

globals.name: SF.readingPosition
globals.summary: The reading position of a scrolling column, the one rule sf-list-feed and sf-list keep a person's place by: create(scroller, {nearEnd, nearStart, onStart}) answers a controller with atEnd(), atStart(), keep(mutate) (content changed above what is read without moving it), toEnd({instant, settle, then}) (smooth unless reduced motion), hold(), release() and check() (call on scroll: onStart once the start is in reach); watchEdge(sentinel, callback, {root, margin}) reports a sentinel coming within reach and answers the way to stop; scrollerOf(node) is the box that scrolls a node (null for the page), the root a watch inside a scroller takes. NEAR_END 96, NEAR_START 240, EDGE_MARGIN 200px. docs/developer/reading-position.md.

globals.name: SF.icons
globals.summary: The icon helpers every set shares. SF.icons.choices: the frozen list of the hundred and twenty glyph names a person chooses from (a record section, a menu row), drawn as sf-dropdown options of kind icon; raised from sf-view-properties (duplication audit 2026-11-03, A-1).

globals.name: SF.language
globals.summary: The page's language and the words registered for components.

globals.name: SF.pageLanguage
globals.summary: The language that applies to a node: the nearest lang.

globals.name: SF.pageText
globals.summary: A component's word in the language of a node, with the page's registered words first.

globals.name: SF.EarlyPort
globals.summary: Ports declared on elements (a <script type="application/json" data-sf-port> island: port, version, url, capabilities, first {intent, payload}): Core sends the first call when it runs, before any component's code, and hands the element the port with connect-port when it is defined; the port's first matching call takes that answer (one request). register(id, adapter) is the page's port registry for an island without a url; start and take are the adoption contract for a product's own adapter (one early answer per port, taken once, matched by port, version, intent and canonical payload, younger than 10 s). docs/developer/early-port.md.

globals.name: SF.ready
globals.summary: The Loader's readiness (simai/ui-source#16), on window.SF as soon as core.js has run. A thenable: await SF.ready (or SF.ready.then) settles with window.SF exactly when the Loader sends sf-loader-init -- SF.Loader, SF.loadSmartBase and the other core-loader names are there by then -- and a script that asks later gets it already settled; it never rejects. One per page: created once on the shared global, kept by every later bundle (a second core.js included) and never replaced. Called as SF.ready(fn), it runs fn once the Loader is up and the document has been parsed, synchronously when both have happened. A script that runs before core.js queues a function with (window.SF_ON_READY = window.SF_ON_READY || []).push(fn); fn is called with window.SF at the same moment.

globals.name: SF.whenDefined
globals.summary: A promise of a Smart element's definition, loading it when the page has not.

globals.name: SF.whenDefine
globals.summary: The older name of SF.whenDefined, kept.

globals.name: SF.whenFieldRenderers

globals.name: SF.tags

globals.name: SF.aliases
globals.summary: Dated aliases of an element (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8 §16.20): install(element, table) keeps a component's old event, setting, attribute, action and value names working until remove_after and notes each use in SF.deprecations with its dates; strict = true withholds expired names.

globals.name: SF.Assembly

The journal records every turn in development mode (?sf-debug). Not yet: undoable steps and slots in the runtime.
